newsitem.title: USA: No antitrust problems in P&G buy--attorneys.
newsitem.headline: No antitrust problems in P&G buy--attorneys.

text.p: Procter & Gamble's proposed purchase of Tambrands Inc poses no real antitrust problems, two lawyers said Wednesday.
Procter & Gamble said Wednesday it plans to buy Tambrands, maker of Tampax tampons, for $1.85 billion or $50 a share.
Procter & Gamble makes sanitary napkins but has not made tampons since its Rely product was pulled from the market in 1980 after it was associated with toxic shock syndrome.
"I would not bet that this will end up being seen as a serious antitrust problem," said Robert Skitol, of the Washington firm of Drinker, Biddle and Reath.
He said the question would be whether tampons and sanitary napkins are considered distinct markets, or whether one is considered a close substitute for the other.
J. Mark Gidley of White & Case in Washington agreed such an acquisition was unlikely to cause any problems.
"There's no direct overlap," he said. "It's really a potential competition issue, and although it may get a lot of scrutiny I'm not sure that there should really be an issue at the end of the day."
